onboarding.title: Welcome to TabRunner
onboarding.tagline: An AI agent that drives this browser — your tabs, your sessions, your logins — to get tasks done.
onboarding.connectPrompt: To start, connect a provider — sign in with a subscription you already pay for, or paste an API key. Either way it stays on this device and goes straight to the provider — there is no TabRunner server.
onboarding.presetsNote: {{count}} presets — Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi, Z.ai, Ollama… — or any compatible endpoint.

settings.defaultStartUrlHint: A task starts on the page you're looking at. When Chrome blocks that page — chrome:// or the Web Store — it opens here instead.
settings.showWidgetHint: A small floating indicator on your tabs while a task runs or waits in line.
settings.showTipsHint: Occasional shortcuts and feature tips under the composer, and while a task runs.
settings.invalidUrl: Enter a full URL starting with http:// or https://
settings.aboutBody: TabRunner is an open-source browser agent: you describe a task, it drives your real browser through the AI provider you choose. Everything is MIT-licensed on GitHub — bugs, ideas and pull requests are welcome.

mcp.title: MCP
mcp.help: Let external AI clients drive this agent through the local bridge — and connect out to remote MCP servers whose tools join every run.
mcp.enableHint: The extension dials out to a local daemon that your AI client starts. Off costs nothing — no port, no wake-ups.
mcp.portHint: Must match the daemon's TABRUNNER_BRIDGE_PORT. Default is 17836.
mcp.invalidPort: Enter a whole number between 1024 and 65535
mcp.guideTitle: How MCP works here — both directions
mcp.guideIn: Clients dial in (the bridge): an external AI client spawns a small local daemon, TabRunner connects out to it, and that client's tasks run in this browser with your logged-in sessions. Off costs nothing.
mcp.guideOut: TabRunner dials out: add an https:// MCP server below and its tools join every run's toolkit — namespaced mcp__server__tool, always behind plan approval. Auth headers stay local and are never logged.
mcp.guideQuestions: Servers can ask questions mid-task; they reach you as a card in the panel (declined automatically on runs nobody watches). Run events can also POST outward as webhooks — see Settings → Behavior.
mcp.statusWaiting: Waiting for the daemon — it starts when your MCP client starts. If nothing connects, check the port above and re-run the setup below.
mcp.setupHelp: Fetch the daemon, then register it with your MCP client:
mcp.extensionIdHint: Set the daemon's TABRUNNER_BRIDGE_EXPECTED_EXTENSION_ID to this.

settings.walkthroughsHint: Let the agent turn a task into a shareable step-by-step walkthrough when you ask it to. Screenshots stay on this computer and are never sent to the model.

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.help: Things TabRunner should always do — or never do — in every chat. Write them like plain sentences. Start a line with "## site: acme.com" to make everything under it apply only on that site.
instructions.placeholder:
Always ask me before sending an email or making a payment.
My work email is me@acme.com.

## site: github.com
Always work in the acme-corp organization.
instructions.autosave: Saved as you type. Takes effect on your next task.

memory.title: What TabRunner remembers
memory.help: Facts TabRunner has picked up from your tasks, so it doesn't have to ask twice. Facts tied to one site load only when a task starts there. Delete anything that's wrong.
memory.empty: Nothing yet. As tasks run, anything worth remembering about you or a site you use lands here on its own — there's nothing to add by hand.
memory.off: Memory is off — TabRunner isn't saving what it learns. Turn it on above to resume.

skills.title: Skills
skills.help: Saved recipes TabRunner offers the model when a task matches — your way of doing a thing, kept. A skill tied to sites is offered only when a task starts there.
skills.empty: No skills yet. A skill is your way of doing a task, written down once — the steps, the quirks, the site. Save one from a chat with /skill new, write one here with New skill, or bring in somebody else's with Import.
skills.deleteDescription: Future tasks won't see it anymore. This can't be undone.

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes — what /skill and the model call it.
form.descriptionHint: What it does and when to use it — this is how the model decides to load it.
form.descriptionPlaceholder: Downloads the newest invoice PDF from the vendor's billing page
form.sitesHint: Comma-separated domains, like acme.com. On those sites it's offered automatically; empty offers it everywhere.
form.bodyPlaceholder: The steps, in order — pages, buttons, fields, and the quirks worth knowing.

import.title: Import a skill
import.description: Fetch a SKILL.md from a URL or GitHub shorthand, or paste one. Nothing saves until you review it.
import.urlHint: A raw .md URL, a GitHub file page, or owner/repo shorthand.
import.review: Review before saving — on matching tasks these instructions are handed to the model as if you wrote them.
import.ignored: Fields TabRunner skills don't use were skipped: {{list}}
import.droppedSites: Site entries that aren't domains were skipped: {{list}}
import.errorHttp: Only https URLs can be imported — an http source could be tampered with in transit. Find an https link and try again.
import.errorUnparseable: That doesn't look like an https URL or an owner/repo shorthand. Check it and try again.
import.errorTimeout: The server didn't answer within 10 seconds — it may be slow or down. Try again in a moment.
import.errorNetwork: The fetch failed — the address may be wrong or the server unreachable. Check the URL and try again.
import.errorStatus: The server answered {{status}} — the file may have moved or be private. Check the URL and try again.
import.errorTooLarge: That file is over 256 KB — too big for a skill. Point at the SKILL.md itself, not an archive.
import.errorEmpty: The server answered with an empty file — check that the URL points at the SKILL.md.
import.errorNothingPasted: Paste the skill's markdown first — frontmatter plus instructions.

draft.title: New skill from this chat
draft.description: TabRunner distills what this chat worked out into a reusable recipe — review and edit before saving.
draft.errorNothing: This chat has nothing to distill yet — run a task first, then save what it worked out.
draft.errorTimeout: The model didn't answer within 90 seconds — it may be overloaded. Try again.
draft.errorEmpty: The model answered with nothing to save. Try again, or write the skill by hand.

errors.badName: Name must be lowercase letters, digits and dashes (like "invoice-download") — and "new" is reserved.
errors.noDescription: A description is required — without one the model never sees the skill.
errors.noBody: Instructions are required — an empty skill teaches nothing.
errors.descriptionTooLong: Description is over {{max}} characters — tighten it; it's a catalog line, not the instructions.
errors.bodyTooLong: Instructions are over {{max}} characters — trim the steps or split into two skills.
errors.nameTaken: A skill named "{{name}}" already exists — pick another name or edit that one.
errors.tooMany: You have {{max}} skills — the cap. Delete one you no longer use before adding another.
No more than {{max}} MCP servers — remove one to add another.
errors.invalidUrl: Enter an https:// URL (plain http:// works for localhost only).
errors.invalidName: Give the server a name of up to 32 characters.
errors.duplicate: A server with this name already exists.

run.serverDown: MCP server "{{name}}" is unreachable — continuing without its tools.

mcpOut.title: Connect to MCP servers
mcpOut.help: Add remote MCP servers whose tools this agent can call during its runs. Every remote tool sits behind plan approval, like page actions.
mcpOut.dialogHelp: The agent lists this server's tools when a run starts and may call them once a plan is approved.
mcpOut.nameHint: Becomes part of tool names — keep it short (letters, digits, dashes).
mcpOut.urlHint: https:// anywhere; plain http:// only for localhost.
mcpOut.headersHint: Sent verbatim with every request. Values stay in this browser's storage and are never logged.
mcpOut.deleteDescription: Its tools leave new runs. Anything already in a transcript stays.
mcpOut.empty: Nothing here yet — this is where TabRunner reaches out, rather than being driven. Add a remote MCP server and its tools join every run's toolkit, each one behind plan approval so nothing fires before you've seen the plan.

errors.tooMany: No more than {{max}} webhooks — remove one to add another.
errors.invalidUrl: Enter an https:// URL (plain http:// works for localhost only).
errors.badEvent: Pick one of the four events.

hooks.title: Webhooks
hooks.help: POST a JSON payload to your own URL when runs start, finish, hit an error, or ask you something. Fire-and-forget — a slow endpoint never holds a run.
hooks.dialogHelp: One event to one URL. The payload is the event's details as JSON; deliveries are single-shot, no retries.
hooks.urlHint: https:// anywhere; plain http:// only for localhost.
hooks.headersHint: Auth headers can be added by editing the rule in storage for now — plain webhooks need none.
hooks.deleteDescription: Future events stop being delivered. Nothing already sent is affected.
hooks.empty: No webhooks yet. Add one and TabRunner pings that URL at the moment you picked — run started, finished, errored, or asking you a question.

schedule.lateNote: This run was scheduled for {{scheduled}} and is starting late, because the browser was closed until now. Take the delay into account, and say so in your summary if it changes the answer.
schedule.historyLostNote: The earlier conversation for this schedule is no longer stored, so there is no record here of what its previous runs found. Treat this as a first run — do not assume any of the work was already done.

errors.pastFire: That time has already passed — pick one in the future.
errors.badDays: days must be numbers from 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday).
errors.badTime: "{{value}}" is not a time — use 24-hour HH:MM, like "09:00".
errors.tooFrequent: A repeating task runs at most every {{min}} minutes.
errors.badWindow: The window's end time has to come after its start.
errors.badRecurrence: recurrence needs a kind of "once", "daily" or "interval", plus the field that kind requires: at, time, or every_minutes.
errors.neverFires: That rule never comes around — check the time and the days.
errors.tooMany: There are already {{max}} scheduled tasks, the most TabRunner keeps. Cancel one before adding another.
errors.selfOnly: A scheduled run can only re-time the schedule it is running from, never create a new one. If new work should be scheduled, ask the user.
errors.chainExhausted: This schedule has rescheduled itself {{max}} times without the user stepping in. Stop here and report what you found.
errors.noTask: task is required — say what the scheduled run should do.
errors.noId: id is required — take it from the scheduled-tasks list.
errors.notFound: No schedule with id {{id}} — it may already be cancelled.

ui.title: Scheduled tasks
ui.help: Work TabRunner runs on its own, in a tab of its own. Each one keeps its own chat, and notifies you when it finishes.
ui.emptyBody: Scheduled tasks run with nobody watching — a morning inbox summary, an hourly price check.
ui.emptyAction: Ask for one in the side panel: “every weekday at 9am, summarize my inbox”. Approve the plan and it appears here.
ui.runNowOnce: Run now as a test — it still fires at its scheduled time
ui.queued: Queued — starts when the current task finishes
ui.pause: Pause — keeps the task and its chat, stops the timer
ui.resume: Resume — the next fire is recalculated from now
ui.deleteRunning: Delete this schedule and stop the task in progress
ui.deleteBody: The rule is removed and nothing else fires. Its chat stays in your history.
ui.deleteBodyRunning: It's running right now — deleting stops the task in progress. Its chat stays in your history.

step.evaluate: Run a script on the page

doc.prerequisite: Before you start: sign in to {{hosts}} with an account that can do this.
doc.notePartial: This task was interrupted, so the walkthrough stops before the process finished.
doc.noteTruncated: The process ran longer than one document holds — the later steps are not shown.
doc.noteLateArm_one: Documenting started after the first action, which is not shown.
doc.noteLateArm_other: Documenting started after the first {{count}} actions, which are not shown.
doc.noteDegraded: Some screens could not be captured on this browser, so a few steps have no picture.
doc.noteStopped: The task was stopped by hand before it finished.
doc.noteFailed: The task ended on an error, so the last step may not have worked.

card.title: Walkthrough
card.review: Check the screenshots before sharing — they show whatever was on screen.

viewer.missingBody: Its screenshots were deleted — a walkthrough goes when its chat does, or when storage fills up.
viewer.missingFix: Run the task again and ask TabRunner to document it.
viewer.emptyBody: The task was documented, but no screen could be captured — the tab was probably closed or blocked before the first shot. Run it again to get a fresh recording.

addProvider.title: Add provider
addProvider.description: Sign in, or paste a key — either one stays on this device and is sent only to the provider.

providerForm.groupSubscription: Subscription — a plan you already pay for
providerForm.groupApiKey: API key — paste a key, billed per use
providerForm.name: Name
providerForm.nameRequired: Give it a name — whatever you'll recognize it by.
providerForm.baseUrlRequired: A custom endpoint needs a base URL.
providerForm.baseUrlInvalid: Base URL isn't a valid URL — include https:// and any path, e.g. https://api.example.com/v1.
providerForm.apiKeyRequired: Paste an API key above. Local endpoints like Ollama don't need one.
providerForm.keyHintKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved key.
providerForm.keyRejected: {{name}} didn't accept this key. Check you copied the whole key and that it belongs to this provider, then try again.
providerForm.modelNote: Model and reasoning effort are picked per task in the side panel — newest model by default.
providerForm.signInHint: Uses your {{provider}} subscription — no API key needed.
providerForm.signInOpened: We opened {{host}} in a new tab. Approve the sign-in there to finish.
providerForm.signInBlocked: If the tab didn't open, use this link:
providerForm.signInExpiredBody: Sign-in links and codes are only valid for a few minutes. Start over to get a fresh one.
providerForm.signInDeniedBody: The request was rejected on the approval page. Start over and approve it to connect {{provider}}.

providerList.emptyBody: A provider is the AI that drives your browser — pick a preset or point at any OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoint.
providerList.removeActiveBody: This is your active provider — the next one in the list becomes active. What TabRunner stored for it, API key or sign-in, is deleted.
providerList.removeBody: TabRunner deletes what it stored for this provider — the API key or the sign-in. You can add it again at any time.
providerList.signOutBody: TabRunner forgets this sign-in and stops using the subscription. The provider stays in your list — sign in again whenever you like.

modelPicker.modelTitle: Model for the next task — Auto picks the newest at run start
modelPicker.modelTitleFor: {{model}} — model for the next task. Auto picks the newest at run start.
modelPicker.noModelListHint: The endpoint didn't return a model list — type an id, or leave empty to auto-pick at run time.
modelPicker.effortHint: Reasoning effort for the next task — an unsupported level fails with a clear provider error in chat.

enginePicker.triggerTitle: {{label}} — provider, model, and effort for the next task
enginePicker.noMatch: No model matches “{{query}}” — clear the filter to see the full list.
enginePicker.moreModels: {{n}} more — narrow the filter to reach them.
enginePicker.thisChatOnly: Hold {{mod}} to change only this chat

usage.title: Subscription usage
usage.empty: The provider didn't report usage this time — try Refresh.

sidepanel.busyRunning: Stop the task before switching chats
sidepanel.close: Close the panel — a running task keeps going

history.title: History
history.ranOnSchedule: Ran on a schedule, not started by you
history.deleteBody: The transcript is deleted from this device and can't be recovered. Anything TabRunner learned from it stays in its memory — you can clear those in Settings.
history.deleteScheduledBody: This is a scheduled task's own chat ({{recurrence}}), and its transcript is what each run reads back. Deleting it cancels the schedule too. To stop it for a while instead, pause it in Settings.
history.emptyBody: Every task you send is kept here — open one to reread what happened, or delete the ones you're done with.
history.storedNote: Stored on this device · the 50 most recent are kept
history.spentTip: Estimated spend on this conversation, at the model's list prices

chat.stopTitleQueued: Stop (Esc) — queued messages run as the next task
chat.sendTitle: Send — Enter · Shift+Enter for a new line
chat.emptyBody: Describe a task and I'll drive the browser — navigate, read pages, click, type — on the page you're looking at, or open its own tab when there's no page to work. Uses your existing logins.
chat.emptyExample: Example: "pull the latest invoice from my inbox into the expense report"
chat.portLost: Lost the connection to the agent, so the task stopped. Send it again to pick up.
chat.reloaded: TabRunner was reloaded — close and reopen this panel to keep going.
chat.runStopped: You stopped this task — your next message can pick up from here.

hint.badKey: Likely a bad or missing API key — update it and try again.
hint.signedOut: The sign-in for this provider is no longer valid — sign in again and retry.
hint.quota: Your plan's usage quota is spent — top up with the provider, or switch to another one and retry.
hint.rateLimited: Rate limited — wait a moment, then send again.
hint.rejected: The provider rejected the request — often an unsupported model or reasoning effort level. The detail above says which.
hint.network: Couldn't reach the provider — check the base URL and your connection.
hint.noProvider: Pick or add one — it takes a minute.

chat.screenshotAlt: Screenshot of the page the agent captured
chat.attachFailed: Couldn't read that image — the format may be unsupported. Copy it again as PNG or JPEG and paste once more.
chat.queueTitle: Inserted between the next tool calls
chat.queuedSteerTitle: Queued for the running task — lands between the next tool calls
chat.queueNoImages: Images can't join a running task — queue the text now and paste the image with the next task.
chat.pasteHint: Long pasted text is folded into a note to keep things tidy — the full text is still sent. Backspace deletes it.
chat.restrictedPageHint: Chrome blocks extensions on this page — your task will run in a tab of its own.
chat.askUserHint: Pick one, or write your own
chat.planPlaceholder: Approve the plan above, or type what should change…
chat.planSendTitle: Send the plan back with your note
chat.planNoImages: Images can't ride a plan note — type what should change, and paste the image once the task is moving.
chat.reasoningToggle: Show or hide the model's reasoning (saved for all chats)
chat.emptyExampleDoc: Add “and document it” to any task and you get a guide you can share.

commands.unknown: No command /{{name}} — type / for the list.
commands.nextTask: Applies to the next task, not the one running.
commands.thisChatOnly: This chat only — new chats keep the default.

deferred.title: Waiting for the task to finish — it fires the moment nothing is working here

stop.none: Nothing is running here — there's no task to stop.
stop.elsewhere: Nothing is running in this chat — the task working now belongs to another one.
stop.cancelledQueued: Took your task out of the queue — nothing was started.

background.description: Toggle whether the next task runs in the foreground or in the background
background.invalid: No setting called “{{value}}” — pick on or off.
background.nowBackground: Next task runs in the background — the panel closes once you approve the plan, and nothing moves your screen after that. Same tab either way.
background.nowForeground: Next task runs in the foreground — the panel stays open and the run brings a tab it switches to forward.

effort.description: Set reasoning effort — none, low, medium, high, max, or default

model.description: Pin the model for this chat — auto undoes it
model.current: Model: {{model}} ({{provider}}) — /model <id> to pin one, /model auto for the endpoint's newest.

rename.description: Name this chat — no argument shows the current name
rename.current: This chat is “{{title}}” — /rename <name> to change it.
rename.none: Send a task first — a chat with no messages has nothing to name.

usage.description: Show the active subscription's usage windows
usage.unsupported: {{provider}} runs on an API key — usage windows only exist for subscription sign-ins (Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi).

mcp.none: No remote MCP servers yet. Add one under Settings → MCP and its tools join every run.

document.description: Run a task and get a shareable step-by-step walkthrough
document.task:
{{task}}

Document this process as a step-by-step walkthrough I can share.
document.hint: Type the task after /document — or add “and document it” to any task.

skill.description: Run a saved skill — /skill new turns this chat into one
skill.none: No skills yet — /skill new turns this chat into one, or import one in Settings → Skills.
skill.disabled: "{{name}}" is disabled — enable it in Settings → Skills.
skill.emptyConversation: Nothing here to turn into a skill yet — run a task first.
skill.taskWithArgs: Use the "{{name}}" skill for this task: {{args}}

compact.description: Summarize this chat so far, to free up context
compact.nothing: Nothing to compact yet — this chat is still short enough to replay in full.
compact.busy: A task is working — compact once it finishes.

keys.recall: Walk back through what you've sent
keys.plan: Expand or collapse every plan card
keys.open: Open help & shortcuts — the composer must be empty

compact.folded: Folded {{count}} earlier turns into a summary to free up context
compact.explain: The messages above stay here for you — the agent replays this summary instead.

context.tooltip: Context: the conversation has spent {{used}} tokens; the model's window is {{window}} — /compact summarizes the chat to free some up
context.tooltipUnknown: Context: the conversation has spent {{used}} tokens. This model's window size isn't known, so there's no percentage to show — /compact summarizes the chat to free some up

plan.title: Plan
plan.peekToggle: Show or hide the whole plan
plan.reapprovalTitle: The plan changed — approve the new one?
plan.revisionNote: The user sent this plan back with requested changes. Call `plan` again with a revised list — it goes back to the user for approval, and no page action runs before that.
plan.narrowedNote: This list dropped steps the run already finished — the progress card lost them. Call `plan` again with the whole arc (finished steps included, cursor past them) unless the user cancelled those steps.

run.drivingTabTip: Show the tab TabRunner is controlling
run.bridgeTask: {{client}} is running a task in your browser
run.bridgeStopTitle: Stops the task and hands the browser back
run.backgroundNowTitle: Close the panel and let this task finish on its own — it never moves your screen. Reopen any time to watch.
run.backgroundNowGated: Approve the plan first — closing now would leave the approval waiting on a notification.
run.modeTitle: “In foreground” keeps the panel open so you can watch, and the run brings a tab it switches to forward; “In background” closes the panel once you approve the plan and never moves your screen. Both drive the tab you're on — flipping mid-task applies at once (once the plan is approved)

queue.queuedTitle: Waiting for the current task to finish

widget.openHint: Watch the run — opens the panel beside the page TabRunner is driving
widget.hideHint: Collapse to a small dot — click the dot to bring the widget back
widget.settledHint: Open TabRunner to see the result

tips.label: Tip
tips.escStop: Esc stops the running task — anything already typed is sent as the next one.
tips.historyRecall: Press ↑ any time to walk back through what you've sent — ↓ comes forward, draft and all.
tips.foreground: Every task works the tab you're looking at — “In background” just closes the panel.
tips.queueSteer: You can keep typing while a task runs — the message queues and steers it between steps.
tips.pasteImage: Paste a screenshot straight into the composer — the agent can see it.
tips.pasteCollapse: A long pasted text folds into a neat token — the full text still reaches the agent.
tips.planApproval: A task shows its plan before it touches the page — approve it, or reply with adjustments and it replans.
tips.planExpand: Press E to expand/collapse the plan.
tips.widget: Every TabRunner mark on a page is clickable — click one to bring the panel back.
tips.board: A task running in another chat shows in the Tasks band at the top — jump to its tab or stop it there.
tips.memory: TabRunner remembers useful facts from your tasks — review or prune them under Settings → Memory.
tips.usage: On a subscription provider, open the model chip in the composer — your 5-hour and weekly usage sit at the bottom.
tips.slashCommands: Type / in the composer for commands — switch provider, model, or effort mid-chat.
tips.compact: Long chat filling up? /compact swaps the older messages for a summary — you keep the scrollback.
tips.schedule: Ask for work on a timer — “every weekday at 9am, check my inbox”. Manage them in Settings.
tips.skills: Taught it something in this chat? /skill new saves the recipe for next time.
tips.siteInstructions: In Instructions, a “## site: acme.com” line scopes everything under it to that site.
tips.enginePicker: The chip by Send sets provider, model, and effort for this chat — /model works too.
tips.engineScope: Each chat keeps its own model and effort — new chats start from your last pick.
tips.help: Press ? on an empty composer for every shortcut and command — /help works too.
tips.walkthrough: Ask “and document it” and the agent writes the process up as a shareable guide.
tips.mcpOut: Type /mcp to see which remote servers answered — add more under Settings → MCP.
tips.webhooks: Run events can POST to your own URL — wire webhooks up under Settings → Behavior.

notify.doneFallback: Task finished — open TabRunner to see how it went.

progress.interrupted: This run was interrupted before it could finish. What it had already done:
progress.stopped: The user stopped this run before it finished. What it had already done:
progress.resume: Call read_history to see these steps' full results, then continue from where it stopped instead of repeating them.
progress.resumeStopped: The user's next message decides what happens to this work — it may continue it or go somewhere else. Call read_history when you need these steps' full results.

errors.alreadyRunningMCP: A task from an external MCP client is already running. Stop it from the client (tabrunner.stop), or wait for it to finish.
errors.alreadyRunningPanel: A task is already running in the TabRunner panel. Open the panel and stop it, or wait for it to finish.
errors.noActiveProvider: No active provider — pick one in the panel dropdown, or add one in Settings.
errors.noActiveTab: No active tab to work with. Click the tab you want, then send the task again.
errors.runCancelled: That queued task was cancelled before it started
errors.tabCreateFailed: Couldn't open a tab for the task: {{message}}
errors.tabClosed: The tab this task was driving ({{title}}) was closed, so the task stopped. TabRunner needs the tab to stay open — reopen the page and send the task again.
errors.outputLimit: The model hit its output limit mid-answer, so this may be cut short — ask it to carry on, or narrow the question.
errors.textOnlyImages: This model can't receive images — the images you attached weren't sent to it. It works from text snapshots of the page.
errors.taskComplete: Finished, but it didn't say what it found. Ask what happened and it'll read back its own steps.
errors.doneLostSummary: You hit the output limit and the closing summary arrived empty. Resume directly — no apology, no recap, no more tool calls. The full analysis is already in this conversation as your earlier message. Call `done` and put that answer in the summary — if it's long, break it into smaller pieces so it isn't cut again.
errors.stepBudgetExhausted: Ran out of steps before finishing. That's the safety cap, not a crash — send the task again to carry on, or narrow it down.
errors.noRunGroup: Couldn't file that tab into a tab group — it may have been closed, or grouping isn't available in this session. You can still switch_tab to it and work there.
errors.tabGroupOtherWindow: That tab is in another window — tab groups can't span windows. You can still switch_tab to it and work there; it just stays outside the group.
errors.historyEmpty: Nothing in the transcript yet — this chat hasn't run a task.
errors.historyNoMatches: Nothing in the transcript matches “{{query}}” — try a shorter phrase.
errors.historyUnavailable: This task has no chat attached — there is no transcript to read.
errors.modelListError: Couldn't load the model list — the endpoint answered {{status}}. {{detail}}
errors.noModel: No model set for {{name}} and the endpoint doesn't list any. Pick a model in Settings.
errors.noModelData: The endpoint answered, but not with a model list. Type a model id yourself, or leave it empty to auto-pick at run time.
errors.kindEntitlement: {{provider}} accepted the key, but your plan doesn't include this API — upgrade the plan on your {{provider}} account
errors.kindQuota: {{provider}} is out of usage — wait for the limit to reset, or top up on your {{provider}} account
errors.kindAuth: {{provider}} rejected the API key — check it or replace it in the provider settings
errors.kindAuthSignedIn: {{provider}} didn't accept the sign-in — sign in again in the provider settings
errors.kindModel: {{provider}} doesn't recognize this model — it may have been renamed or removed; pick another one
errors.kindRate: {{provider}} is rate-limiting requests — try again in a moment
errors.kindRateWindow: {{provider}} hit your {{window}} usage limit — it resets {{reset}}
errors.kindOverload: {{provider}} is overloaded right now — try again in a few minutes
errors.kindContext: This chat outgrew what {{provider}} can read in one request — compact it to carry on
errors.compactEmpty: The model returned an empty summary, so nothing was compacted. Try again, or start a new chat to reset the context.
errors.oauthRefreshExpired: Your {{name}} sign-in expired and couldn't be renewed — sign in again in Settings.
errors.signInRateLimited: The provider's sign-in service is turning requests down right now — too many in a short window. This isn't about your plan's usage. Wait a minute, then start over.
errors.signInRateLimitedFor: The provider's sign-in service is turning requests down right now — too many in a short window. This isn't about your plan's usage. Try again in about {{seconds}}s.
errors.signInTokenResponse: The sign-in response came back incomplete — no usable token. Start over to try again.
errors.signInDeviceResponse: The sign-in service replied in a format TabRunner didn't recognize. Try again in a moment.
errors.noResponseBody: The provider sent an empty response.
errors.restrictedPage: TabRunner can't read this page — Chrome blocks extensions on chrome:// and Web Store pages. Navigate the tab to a regular page and resend the task.
errors.pageNavigating: The page was still loading or navigating — wait for it to settle and retry.
errors.snapshotFailed: Couldn't read the page — it may have navigated, or it's one Chrome blocks (chrome://, Web Store). Try again once it settles.
errors.refNotFound: Element ref "{{ref}}" not found. Run snapshot first to get fresh refs.
errors.notAField: That element can't be filled ({{tag}}) — click buttons, checkboxes and radios instead.
errors.captureEmpty: Nothing captured yet — capture starts when the run attaches to the tab (its first action, screenshot, or evaluate). Trigger what you want to see, then read again.
errors.noTabAttached: Not attached to a tab yet — attach to one before acting on the page.
errors.noHistoryBack: This tab has nothing to go back to — its history starts here. Navigate to the page you want instead.
errors.closeDrivenTab: That is the tab you are driving — switch_tab to another one first, then close it.
errors.findEmpty: find needs something to look for — pass a word or phrase from the page, or call snapshot to see the whole tree.
errors.pageTextReadPartial: Read {{count}} of {{total}} characters of page text
errors.tabOpenFailed: Couldn't open a new tab. Navigate the current one there instead, or try again.
errors.planEmpty: The plan needs at least one step — pass a non-empty list of short phrases.
errors.planRejected: Plan rejected — nothing on the page was touched.
errors.planGate: Blocked — the plan needs your approval first
errors.planGateModel: Blocked: no plan is approved yet. Call the plan tool with your intended steps first; the user must approve the plan before any page action runs.
errors.memoryEmpty: Nothing to remember — pass the fact as a sentence.
errors.usageUnreadable: The provider's usage reply came back in a format TabRunner didn't recognize — try Refresh.
errors.documentUnavailable: Documenting is off — turn on Walkthroughs in Settings, then ask again.
